correctness.rationale: For every legal model, contradiction antecedents have selections wholly in the anti-logical region by id. Boolean factorization of the negated query matrix follows by recording selected worlds and consequent failures. A universally true query row requires a nonempty selected world whose Boolean factor is zero under SCP1, forcing a +1 rank lower bound. Conversely an optimal Boolean factorization, with one extra all-true witness if needed, is realized with arbitrary anti-logical full-formula valuations. An induction on formula complexity legally extends selections to every formula, independently confirming id, soc-m, sic, ne and rl. Identity and zero-plus-singleton rows give matching sharp worst-case examples for all positive parameters. The actual included checker exhaustively verified 5,050 small matrices, semantic realizations for 682 cases, and 196 sharpness constructions. The general proof, not the enumeration, is decisive.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 semantics require globally nonempty counterpossible selections and explicitly motivate a sufficiently rich anti-logical region without quantifying its size. The result solves a natural resource invariant for joint finite counterpossible observations: a complete computable (via classical Boolean rank) exact per-table minimum, a sharp worst-case bound depending on the number of consequents, and a precise one-world distinction between vacuous and nonvacuous semantics. The all-true-row surcharge is a structural witness-cost boundary, not a mere relabeling of matrix rank; the semantic full-language realization is independently proved. This is valuable as exact finite-model sizing and an impossibility test for a given witness budget, although it is not a broad axiomatization or a novel Boolean-rank theorem.
